review_basis: Read complete revision 5 policy, the Astra revision 4 finding, the six new cycle claims and all retained SQL definitions/proofs. Mechanically matched all 28 SQL obligation symbols/statements to spec/sql-types.json.
Registered production baseline comparison returned no changes. Reviewed current pre-refinement proxy state/ReadyForQuery handling without editing it.

Checked official PostgreSQL 16 protocol and settings documentation, including one Ready per Sync, extended-query error skipping, Execute not emitting Ready by itself, and UPDATE pg_settings being equivalent to SET.

Read Terra 2's protocol-name collision finding and the root final-rev5 formal report; the report records VERIFIED with 112 total propositions, 28 SQL propositions, and no production changes at freeze. This seat did not independently run Lean.
approval_basis: The effect barrier repairs the indirect pg_settings path without assuming that a settings-name blacklist covers all aliases/rules or trusted-routine effects. New source-bearing Q/P is rejected while forwarded Q/E effects remain pending.

Marking an effect before forwarding prevents an asynchronous backend reply from opening a window. Validating lexical ParameterStatus before releasing the matching completed barrier prevents later SQL from being admitted under stale lexical assumptions.

Cycle-specific release retains newer effects: E in cycle 0, Sync 0, then E in cycle 1 must leave cycle 1 pending when Ready for cycle 0 arrives. CommandComplete, PortalSuspended, ErrorResponse and Flush alone do not release the source barrier.

Existing admitted Bind/Execute, Sync/Flush, COPY progress and cancellation retain a completion path. New-source pipelining can be conservatively rejected and closed without promising pipeline throughput or retrying accepted effects.
Revision 4's native PREPARE/EXECUTE admission, immutable cache classification, conservative names and shared admitted namespace remain approvable under the previously recorded conditions.
required_implementation_acceptance_condi: Maintain pending effect cycles separately from the initial readiness event. Mark Q/E pending synchronously before any await that can expose forwarding; bind each ReadyForQuery to the ordered Q/Sync boundary that actually generated it. Never clear all pending effects on any Ready, CommandComplete or error.

For the adversarial trace E0, Sync0, E1, delayed Ready0, Pnew, reject Pnew before parser admission/backend forwarding while preserving pending E1. Then test completion of E1 plus its own Sync/Ready permits later source on a session that has never been rejected.

Check delayed/fragmented unsafe ParameterStatus before matching Ready release. Exercise indirect pg_settings changes followed by Q and by P, multiple E in one cycle, old Ready after newer E, errors and skip-until-Sync, transaction Ready statuses I/T/E, COPY completion, cancellation and conservative connection closure.
Treat a rejected session as closed: no later Ready can revive it. Preserve the distinction between rollback of its unfinished transaction and previously committed autocommit work.

Conservatively reject protocol prepared-statement names longer than 63 UTF-8 bytes, or implement PostgreSQL's truncation/collision behavior exactly. Exact protocol strings alone are insufficient when backend names alias at the 63-byte boundary. Cover Parse, Bind statement references and statement Close/Describe, including native/protocol cross-use and equal 63-byte prefixes.

Retain exact ordered singleton statement-family plus leading PREPARE/EXECUTE token checks, all-production restrictions and safe expression policy for native requests. Keep SQL identifier folding separate from exact protocol names; do not let cache hits fabricate preparation or known targets.

Test native unknown/quoted/Unicode/overlong names, duplicate-name/backend failures, both cross-protocol directions and state limits. bodyPart remains a substring-only premise; parser-selected body spans, SQL classification and name normalization require trusted adapter checks.

Complete independent real PostgreSQL, per-client routing counters, full unchanged ACL-bearing pg_dump/pg_restore, migration repair, retrieval integrity and HTTP checks after implementation. Bind final evidence to stable daemon PID/start identity, matching loaded input hashes and the pinned parser binary, rejecting STALE_RUNTIME.
formal_limits: CycleState contains only pending natural-number IDs. forwardEffect blocks source and completeCycle retains newer IDs, but correct cycle assignment, legitimate acknowledgement IDs and truthful lexical-status validation are supplied by the runtime adapter.

The six cycle claims do not prove backend message order, coroutine scheduling, network framing, event/state transitions, actual settings stability or Python refinement. An arbitrary too-new acknowledgement could release state in the abstract model; implementation must establish correspondence to ordered real Q/Sync barriers.
Native body classification/span/name extraction, backend successful preparation, prepared-object lifecycle and cache/namespace correspondence remain outside the Lean claims.

Formal report observation and this design approval do not substitute for post-implementation runtime/recovery evidence. Local execution authorization does not resolve redistribution or commercial licensing.
approval_scope: Exact revision 5 bounded design and abstract-model scope. Implementation acceptance remains conditional on the explicit finite runtime checks above.
